explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the Project Type and Purpose  
   - This is a full-stack web application (“AI 视频图文创作助手”) that lets users load video/audio in the browser, extracts speech via in-browser and backend processing, runs AI models to generate styled text (notes, summaries, subtitles, mind-maps), and presents results in the UI.  
   - Frontend: Vue 3 + Vite + ffmpeg-WASM for client-side media processing.  
   - Backend: Python (Flask/FastAPI-style monolith) exposing REST endpoints, with action modules for ASR, LLM prompts, and task orchestration.  
   - Orchestrated via Docker and Docker-Compose for one-click local deployment.

2. Analyze the File Structure  
   - Top level:  
     • docker-compose.yaml + variables.env → orchestrates two containers (frontend & backend)  
     • Makefile → build & run commands  
     • README files in root, frontend/, backend/ → setup & env instructions  
   - frontend/  
     • Dockerfile, .env.* → containerize static server and Vite dev server  
     • src/ → Vue components, services for API calls (asrService, chatService, markdownService, uploadService) and utils (ffmpeg.js)  
   - backend/  
     • Dockerfile, .pre-commit, requirements.txt → containerize Python service  
     • main.py → API router  
     • actions/ (asr.py, llm.py, dispatcher.py) → business logic for media transcription, LLM calls, task dispatch  
     • constants.py, env.py → configuration loader  
     • No external DB – tasks and metadata stored in local FS or in-memory  

3. Examine README Insights  
   - Core flow diagram (`docs/images/process_flow.jpg`) shows:  
     1. Client uploads video/audio  
     2. Backend runs ASR → transcript  
     3. Backend calls LLM to generate styled document  
     4. Client can chat further with AI on the processed content  
     5. Output: markdown, subtitles  
   - Tech stack: ffmpeg-WASM, Python, AI Model APIs (e.g., Volcengine, OpenAI, etc.), Docker.

4. How to Draw the System Design Diagram  
   a. Main Components  
      - Browser Client (Vue UI + ffmpeg-WASM)  
      - Frontend Server (Vite or static‐file server container)  
      - Backend Service (Python monolith container)  
      - External AI Services (ASR provider, LLM provider)  
      - Local Persistence (file store for task caching, subtitles)  
      - Docker Compose as orchestrator  
   b. Relationships & Data Flow  
      1. User interacts with Vue UI → selects video/audio.  
      2. Client uses ffmpeg-WASM to preprocess or extract segments.  
      3. Client → HTTP(S) upload to Backend `/upload` endpoint.  
      4. Backend dispatcher orchestrates:  
         • calls ASR module → external ASR API → receives transcript  
         • calls LLM module → external LLM API → generates styled document  
         • persists results locally  
      5. Backend → returns JSON payload to Frontend.  
      6. Frontend renders panels (transcription, generated content) and enables AI chat (`/chat` endpoint).  
   c. Architectural Patterns & Design Principles  
      - Client-server separation (thin client handling media, server for AI calls)  
      - Modular monolith on the backend (action modules grouped by responsibility)  
      - Containerization for environment consistency and one-click deployment  
      - Event-driven UI via eventBus.js for component decoupling  
   d. Key Technologies & Libraries  
      - Frontend: Vue 3, Vite, ffmpeg-WASM, eventBus, md5 hashing utility  
      - Backend: Python 3.x, Flask/FastAPI, requests (to AI APIs), throttled-py (rate-limiting), local FS for storage  
      - DevOps: Docker, Docker-Compose, Makefile  

5. Tailor the Diagram for This Full-Stack App  
   - Draw two main service boxes side by side:  
     • Frontend Container (port 3000 or 5173)  
     • Backend Container (port 8080)  
   - Inside Frontend box, subdivide:  
     • UI Components (UploadSection, TranscriptionPanel, GeneratedContentPanel, ChatPanel)  
     • Services Layer (uploadService, asrService, chatService, markdownService)  
     • WASM Engine (ffmpeg.js)  
   - Inside Backend box, subdivide:  
     • API Router (main.py)  
     • Dispatcher → Action Modules (asr.py, llm.py, tos.py)  
     • Config & Env Loader (env.py, constants.py)  
     • Local Storage (tasks/, subtitles/, logs)  
   - Outside both, draw External Services:  
     • ASR API Provider  
     • LLM API Provider  
   - Surround both boxes with a Docker-Compose orchestrator icon.

6. Diagramming Guidelines  
   - Use clear rectangular “containers” for Frontend, Backend, External Services.  
   - Label all components and sub-systems.  
   - Use directional arrows:  
     • Browser → Frontend container (static asset fetch)  
     • Browser ↔ Backend container (REST calls)  
     • Backend → External AI Services (ASR, LLM)  
     • Backend → Local Storage (FS)  
     • Frontend → WASM Engine  
   - Color code:  
     • Blue for UI/client components  
     • Green for backend modules  
     • Red/orange for external third-party services  
   - Shape variations:  
     • Cylinders for storage  
     • Clouds for external AI services  
     • Containers for Docker-Compose elements

7. Essential Details to Capture  
   - Separation of concerns between client preprocessing (ffmpeg-WASM) and server AI orchestration  
   - The pipeline: Upload → ASR → LLM → Client display  
   - One-click local deployment via Docker-Compose  
   - Extensibility: adding new action modules in `backend/actions/`  
   - Rate-limiting via `throttled-py` to protect cloud quotas  

By following the above breakdown and visual guidelines, you’ll produce a clear, complete, and accurate system design diagram that reflects the precise architecture of this AI-powered video-to-document web tool. 
</explanation>
